admin.market.intro: Every ticker and FX pair ever used accumulates daily prices, dividends and splits, is checked for gaps against its exchange calendar (gaps are re-read; days the source lacks are marked, never filled) and is fully re-read monthly. Prices are stored unadjusted; total return is computed here and checked against the source.
admin.sources.intro: US statements come straight from the SEC's official XBRL data: every document is kept as fetched, every filed number accumulates, and restatements keep both values.
admin.sources.secContactHelp: The SEC requires an organisation name and an e-mail on every request; both are needed. They are only sent to the SEC, as a contact.

market.note.adjusted_mismatch: The total return computed here differs from the source's adjusted close and needs review. Common causes: the source applies a dividend in the wrong currency (e.g. declared in USD, traded in HKD) or misses a rights issue. The system computes total return itself from unadjusted prices and dividends.
market.note.source_usd_dividend: The source's adjusted close deducts dividends declared in USD as if they were HKD (about 7.8 times too little). The system checked each ex-date and reproduces the source's figures by repeating that mistake; its own total return uses the HKD dividend and is the correct figure.
market.note.no_source_adjusted: The source has no adjusted prices to check against.

check.title: Data checks
check.intro: Every period is checked against check rules {version}; the letter under each column is its data quality: A all passed, B warnings, C errors.
check.yahoo: Cross-checked against Yahoo figures fetched {at} (unofficial, for reference only).
check.noYahoo: No second-source figures yet, so no cross-source check.
check.allPassed: Every check passed for the periods shown.
check.grade.B: B: warnings; usable, but take note
check.grade.C: C: errors; a valuation should not use these as they are
check.balance_total: Total assets = total liabilities and equity
check.balance_parts: Total assets = total liabilities + total equity
check.gross_profit: Gross profit = revenue − cost of revenue
check.net_income_split: Net income = shareholders' share + non-controlling interests
check.eps_diluted: Diluted EPS ≈ net income to shareholders ÷ diluted shares
check.cost_of_revenue_not_negative: Cost of revenue should not be negative
check.capex_not_negative: Capital expenditure (a payment) should not be negative
check.revenue_jump: Revenue differs from the previous period by over 20× (possibly a unit error)
check.total_assets_jump: Total assets differ from the previous period by over 20× (possibly a unit error)
check.quarters_add_up: Four quarters add up to the year
std.item.claims_reserves: Reserves for claims and claim expenses
check.net_interest_income: Net interest income = interest income − interest expense
check.bank_revenue: Net revenue = net interest income + non-interest income
check.loan_allowance_not_negative: The loan-loss allowance should not be negative
check.net_interest_income_jump: Net interest income differs from the previous period by over 20× (possibly a unit error)
check.insurance_pretax: Pre-tax income = revenue − benefits, claims and expenses (does not hold for every insurer; a note only)
check.premiums_not_negative: Premiums earned should not be negative
ratio.roic: Return on invested capital (ROIC, after-tax operating income ÷ average invested capital)
ratio.cash_conversion: Cash conversion (operating cash flow ÷ net income)
ratio.shareholder_return_to_fcf: Shareholder returns (dividends + buybacks) to free cash flow
ratio.nii_to_assets: Net interest income ÷ average total assets
ratio.loss_ratio: Loss ratio (benefits and claims ÷ premiums earned)
ratio.investment_yield: Investment yield (net investment income ÷ average investments)
std.ratiosIntro: Ratio rules {version}. Ratios with average balances (ROE, ROA …) use the period end and a year earlier, so they are annual and TTM only. Select a number to see its inputs.
std.growthIntro: Quarters compare with the same quarter a year earlier; not shown when the earlier value is zero or negative.
std.cagr: Compound annual growth (to the latest fiscal year)
std.commonNote: Common size: income and cash-flow items as % of revenue, balance-sheet items as % of total assets; per-share figures and share counts do not apply.

cmp.name: Name
opt.title: Portfolio optimizer
opt.subtitle: Up to 10 assets, long only, on total return in your display currency; results are reproducible with a fixed seed.
opt.method: Method: tens of thousands of portfolios are sampled on a 1 % grid within each asset's bounds and scored; the best few are refined with SLSQP and rounded back to whole percents. A composite score standardises each metric (z-score) before weighting.
opt.runInfo: {start} to {end}, {days} common trading days · {samples} portfolios · seed {seed} · {ccy} · {freq} · data {data}
opt.refined: SLSQP refinement found a better portfolio than the samples.
opt.notRefined: The best sampled portfolio was already the best (refinement did not improve it).
opt.savedPortfolio: Saved portfolio “{name}”; add it on the Compare page.
opt.oosIntro: The weights are found on the first part of the period and then held unchanged through the rest, next to an equal-weight portfolio; much weaker results later suggest the optimisation fitted the past too closely.
opt.frontierIntro: Each dot is a sampled portfolio; the line is the highest return at each level of risk; ◆ is the best weights, and each asset held alone is labelled.
opt.scenariosIntro: Saving a scenario computes it once more and records the inputs, the exact data window, the data fingerprint, the seed, the result and the system version; you can recompute it over the same window at any time.
opt.check.identical: ✓ Recomputed identically: same data, weights and score.
opt.check.differentSame: Same data but a different result (the system version may have changed).
opt.check.dataChanged: Data in the window has been revised (e.g. the source corrected a price), so the result may differ.
